newsitem.title: USA: Compass Bancshares expects 96 to meet goals.
newsitem.headline: Compass Bancshares expects 96 to meet goals.

text.p: Compass Bancshares Inc said Thursday it was able to position itself to minimize the effect of a one-time charge to replenish the Savings Association Insurance Fund, and expects to close the 1996 fiscal year having met its goals.
The company did not specify the earnings goals it had set, and did not immediately return a telephone call.

"We continue to experience growth in core earnings fueled by increases in loan outstandings, a stable net interest margin, continued strength in our fee-based business and excellent credit quality," Chairman and Chief Executive Paul Jones said in a statement.
"The growth we have accomplished through internal sources, coupled with our acquisition strategy, give us reasons for optimism as we close 1996 and enter 1997," he added.
The company took a one-time $7.6 million charge against its third quarter earnings as its assessment to recapitalize the Savings Association Insurance Fund.
The charge amounted to $0.13 per share, the company said later Thursday.
A company spokesman later Thursday declined to release its earnings goals for the 1996 fiscal year, saying Compass considers the information proprietary.
